description: A soft, charcoal-grey henley with the sleeves pushed up.  You've worn some version of this shirt for about a century.
A well-cut dark jacket in waxed canvas and leather, expensive and a little battered.

variants.description: A well-cut dark jacket in waxed canvas and leather, expensive and a little battered.

description: Several necklaces worn together: leather cords, a small silver pendant, beads.  Trinkets gathered over a thousand years, and you won't say where any of them came from.
A heavy silver ring engraved with an old Norse knotwork pattern.  You wear it because you like it; the ring that keeps you alive in daylight is the other one.
A thick leather-bound sketchbook full of your charcoal drawings: faces, wolves, the bayou, a little girl with your eyes.  Sketching in it calms you (read it).
A stake carved from the last of the white oak.  The only thing in the world that can kill an Original, including you.  You hid it so well that you sometimes worry you'll forget where.  You never do.

An ornate silver dagger, its blade dulled with white oak ash.  Driven into an Original's heart, it puts them into a dead sleep until someone pulls it out.  You've used these on every one of your siblings.
Very old, very good bourbon from the bar at the Abattoir.  It's the one thing about America you've never complained about.
A heavy, dark-banded ring set with a lapis lazuli stone, spelled by a witch a thousand years ago so that you and your siblings could walk in the sun.  Take it off in daylight and you burn.

A smooth, pale grey stone that seems faintly luminous in the dark.  The curse of the sun and the moon is bound into it, and it's one of the five things you need to break it.  You've waited centuries to hold it.

Your own drawing, done in 1492 in England: a dark-haired young woman with a sly smile.  Katerina Petrova, the doppelganger whose blood was meant to break your curse, before she turned herself into a vampire to escape you.  Her line lives on somewhere.
An oil painting in your own hand: Elijah in his suit, Rebekah laughing, Kol scowling, Finn pretending not to be there, and you at the edge of it all.  Always and forever.

variants.description: An oil painting in your own hand: Elijah in his suit, Rebekah laughing, Kol scowling, Finn pretending not to be there, and you at the edge of it all.  Always and forever.

description: A brass nameplate pried from one of the Mikaelson coffins.

variants.description: "ELIJAH".  The noble one.  He always forgives you, eventually.
"REBEKAH".  She'll be furious when she wakes up.  She always is.
"KOL".  The reckless one.  Daggered for a century, give or take.
"FINN".  The eldest, and the dullest.  Nine hundred years in a box.
